question: Assuming Gareth Evan's Generality Constraint, if I understand a proposition Fa, should I be able to understand Fx (\forall x)? Assume I understand universal quantification.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Yes, under Evans' Generality Constraint (GC), understanding Fa (plus universal quantification) suffices for understanding ∀x Fx. GC requires that grasp of a predicate F is intrinsically general: if one can think Fa, one must be able to recombine F with any other object of thought (Fb, Fc, …) one can entertain. Given competence with the quantifier, this recombinability directly yields the capacity to think the universally quantified content ∀x Fx, whose truth-conditions are exhausted by F holding of every object in the domain.

(The constraint does not demand that one possess a name for every object; it only demands that F be deployable with any singular concept one does possess, which, together with the quantifier, generates the universal thought.)

This enforces recombinability of the same predicate-concept with different singular constituents. By contrast, ∀x Fx is a single general (quantified) thought, not a singular instance. Even if universal quantification is already mastered as a device, nothing in GC forces the thinker to be able to apply F to every object in the domain at once; they need only be able to apply it to any one object they can already single out. Hence understanding Fa is compatible with failing to understand ∀x Fx.

(The constraint is silent on the further cognitive step of generalising the predicate over an entire range.)
